question: What mental strategies can copywriters use to overcome resistance when sending client pitches?
transcript_excerpt: Copywriters can break the resistance into smaller chunks—for example, sending a pitch then taking a break, or setting a timer for focused work followed by a break. Creating external constraints like a deadline (meeting at 4pm means pitches must be sent by 3:42pm) forces completion. Using streaks—committing to send pitches every day for a month or a year—leverages the psychological motivation to not break the streak. Templates and pre-written pitches also remove friction from the process.

question: What apps has the Comprehensive Copywriting Academy released to help students with copywriting tasks?
transcript_excerpt: CCA Plus released apps designed to guide students through creating pitches without writing the pitches for them. The apps provide friendly opening line suggestions and step-by-step guidance so that when students sit down to write a pitch and don't know where to start, they have a framework to follow. The apps were released to the CCA Plus community to help students make the copywriting process faster, better, and easier.

question: How can breaking large copywriting projects into smaller sections improve productivity?
transcript_excerpt: Instead of writing an entire homepage in one session, break it into smaller components like writing just the headline, or focusing on one section at a time. This approach mirrors the mental framing of running three separate 5-kilometer chunks instead of one 15-kilometer run. By working on discrete sections, copywriters reduce overwhelm and can apply the same mental tricks—finishing one small section motivates completion of the next.

question: Why should copywriters create invoice templates rather than building from scratch each time?
transcript_excerpt: Having a go-to invoice template means you don't have to rebuild the document every time—you just fill in your numbers and send. This removes friction from a task many copywriters resist completing. The same principle applies to other administrative copywriting work: use templates so you can focus on customization rather than creating structure from zero, making it easier to actually send invoices and get paid.

question: What is the difference between planning and pantsing in creative writing, and why is the distinction not always black and white?
transcript_excerpt: Some writers plan everything with detailed outlines, while others 'fly by the seat of their pants' and discover the story as they write. However, many authors use a hybrid approach—one published author mentioned she simply has characters she likes and a place to put them, then writes to see where it goes. Kate Sitarz uses a 'puzzle pieces' approach, writing individual scenes that may eliminate or build off each other. The key is being playful and serious about goals while trusting your own process rather than following rigid writing dogma.
